Rules: real_exam/TEACHING_STYLE_GUIDE.md R1-R35 (no 'which way is better' verdict) + NITZAN_RHYTHM_DELIVERY.md P1-P13. Calm preset on the question reading and plain calculations.

slides.say: A food truck offers seven soups and three kinds of bread. A lunch contains one soup and one kind of bread. How many different lunches are possible?
So they ask how many lunches, not how many items. A lunch is a pair, one soup and one bread.
at: So they ask how many lunches

slides.say: Let's solve it the math way, in stages, like in the lesson. We have two stages of choice, the soup and the bread.
The soup has seven options. We write seven in its box.
at: We write seven in its box

slides.say: The bread has three options. We write three in its box.
at: We write three in its box

slides.say: Why do we multiply? Take the first soup. With it, we can take any of the three breads. That's three lunches.
The second soup also goes with three breads. Three more lunches.
And so on for all seven soups. Three lunches for each soup, seven times.
Three, seven times, is seven times three. That's twenty-one lunches.
Careful here. A lot of students add, seven plus three is ten. That's choice number one. But ten counts the items on the menu, not the lunches.
And if we start with the bread? Each bread goes with seven soups. Three times seven is twenty-one again. The order of the stages doesn't matter.
Choice number two is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number two is our answer
